learningObjectives.title: The end of the Second World War: Yalta, Potsdam and the atomic bomb
The Iron Curtain and the evolution of East-West rivalry
The development of the Cold War: superpower rivalry in Asia and Europe
Military and nuclear rivalry: tension over Cuba and Germany

questions.q: When was the Yalta Conference held?
options: February 1945
July 1945
August 1945
February 1946
questions.explain: The Yalta Conference met in February 1945 while the war in Europe was still being fought.

questions.q: Which American president represented the USA at the Potsdam Conference?
options: Franklin D. Roosevelt
Harry Truman
Dwight Eisenhower
Woodrow Wilson
questions.explain: Roosevelt had died in April 1945, so Truman represented the USA at Potsdam in July 1945.

questions.q: Why were relations between the superpowers more strained at Potsdam than at Yalta?
options: Roosevelt had been replaced by the more anti-communist Truman, and the USA had tested the atomic bomb
Stalin had been replaced by Khrushchev
Germany had not yet surrendered
The USA had joined the Warsaw Pact
questions.explain: By Potsdam the hard-line Truman had replaced Roosevelt and the USA had successfully tested the atomic bomb, deepening distrust.

questions.q: What was one effect of the USA dropping the atomic bomb in 1945 on superpower relations?
options: It increased Soviet distrust of the USA and encouraged the USSR to develop its own bomb
It immediately ended all tension between the superpowers
It persuaded Stalin to hold free elections in Eastern Europe
It led the USA to disband its armed forces
questions.explain: The bomb heightened Soviet suspicion and spurred the USSR to build its own atomic weapon, fuelling the arms race.

questions.q: Who delivered the 'Iron Curtain' speech in 1946?
options: Winston Churchill
Harry Truman
Joseph Stalin
George Kennan
questions.explain: Churchill warned that an 'iron curtain' had descended across Europe in his speech at Fulton, Missouri in March 1946.

questions.q: In which year were both the Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan announced?
questions.explain: Both the Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan were announced in 1947.

questions.q: What was the main aim of the Marshall Plan?
options: To provide US economic aid to rebuild Europe and resist the spread of communism
To create a military alliance against the USSR
To divide Germany into four zones of occupation
To supply nuclear weapons to Western Europe
questions.explain: The Marshall Plan offered dollars to rebuild European economies, making communism less appealing.

questions.q: A Soviet newspaper in 1947 described Marshall Aid as a tool of American control. Which interpretation does this best support?
options: Stalin saw the plan as 'dollar imperialism' designed to extend US influence over Europe
Stalin welcomed the aid for the Soviet Union
The plan was intended to strengthen the Warsaw Pact
The plan aimed to reunify Germany under Soviet control
questions.explain: Stalin viewed Marshall Aid as 'dollar imperialism' and forbade Eastern bloc states from accepting it.

questions.q: When did the Berlin Blockade begin?
options: June 1948
May 1949
June 1950
August 1961
questions.explain: Stalin began the Berlin Blockade in June 1948, cutting off land routes into West Berlin.

questions.q: Why did Stalin impose the Berlin Blockade in 1948?
options: To force the Western Allies out of Berlin, partly in response to a new currency in the western zones
To punish West Germany for joining NATO
To retaliate for the building of the Berlin Wall
To prevent the Marshall Plan from reaching the USSR
questions.explain: Stalin hoped to drive the Allies out of Berlin after they merged their zones and introduced the new Deutsche Mark.

questions.q: In which year was NATO founded?
questions.explain: NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, was formed in 1949 as a Western defensive alliance.

questions.q: Why did the superpowers become involved in the Korean War from 1950?
options: The USA acted to contain communism after North Korea invaded the South, while the USSR and China backed the North
Both superpowers sent troops to reunify Korea as a democracy
The war was fought only between Korea and Japan
The USA supported communist North Korea against the capitalist South
questions.explain: The USA led a UN force to contain communism after the communist North invaded the South, with the USSR and China backing the North.

questions.q: Why did the USSR crush the Hungarian Uprising in 1956?
options: To stop Hungary leaving the Warsaw Pact and to maintain Soviet control of Eastern Europe
To force Hungary to accept Marshall Aid
To reunite Hungary with Austria
To install a capitalist government in Hungary
questions.explain: Khrushchev sent in troops when Nagy announced Hungary would leave the Warsaw Pact, to preserve Soviet dominance of the Eastern bloc.

questions.q: A textbook states the Warsaw Pact was created as a direct reaction to a Western decision. Which decision was it?
options: West Germany was allowed to rearm and join NATO in 1955
The USA dropped the atomic bomb
The Berlin Wall was built
The Marshall Plan was announced
questions.explain: The Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955 in response to West Germany being rearmed and admitted to NATO.

questions.q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
questions.explain: The Berlin Wall was constructed in August 1961.

questions.q: Why did the East German government build the Berlin Wall?
options: To stop the large numbers of refugees fleeing from East to West Berlin
To protect East Berlin from a NATO invasion
To block Marshall Aid entering the city
To reunite the two halves of Berlin
questions.explain: The Wall was built to halt the flow of skilled refugees escaping communist East Germany through West Berlin.

questions.q: Who was the American U-2 spy plane pilot shot down over the USSR in 1960?
options: Gary Powers
John F. Kennedy
George Kennan
Fidel Castro
questions.explain: Gary Powers was captured when his U-2 was shot down, wrecking the Paris Peace Summit.

questions.q: In October 1962 Soviet ships turned back and the USSR agreed to remove its missiles from Cuba. Which conclusion does this best support?
options: The Cuban Missile Crisis was widely seen as a diplomatic success for Kennedy and the USA
The USSR had gained a permanent nuclear base in Cuba
The USA agreed to invade Cuba
The crisis triggered a full nuclear war
questions.explain: Khrushchev's agreement to withdraw the missiles was seen as a US victory, though the USA secretly agreed to remove its missiles from Turkey.

questions.q: Who led the reform movement known as the 'Prague Spring' in Czechoslovakia in 1968?
options: Alexander Dubček
Leonid Brezhnev
Imre Nagy
Nikita Khrushchev
questions.explain: Dubček introduced reforms ('socialism with a human face'), which were crushed when Warsaw Pact forces invaded in August 1968.

questions.q: What is meant by 'détente' in the period leading up to 1972?
options: An easing of tension between the superpowers, reflected in agreements such as SALT 1
A sharp escalation of the nuclear arms race
The complete collapse of communism in Europe
A military alliance between the USA and the USSR
questions.explain: Détente meant a relaxation of Cold War tension, shown by the SALT 1 treaty limiting nuclear weapons in 1972.
